author: N. A. Naylor
title: Central 301 highlights sports events and recognizes staff in latest social media posts
text:
Central 301, the official account for Central Community Unit School District 301, shared updates this week on school sports events, student traditions, and staff appreciation across its district in Kane and DeKalb counties.
On May 5, Central 301 posted about a series of athletic competitions taking place that day: “LUNCHTIME LINEUP: We have boys lacrosse & softball taking on that school up north. Plus girls soccer hosts Huntley. Finally, a special baseball matchup with Richmond-Burton in a game at Wintrust Field in Schaumburg! TICKETS: https://t.co/kIKsZTFXIx #WeAreCentral”
The following day, May 6, the district highlighted the contributions of its nursing staff with the message: “They’re the first stop when something isn’t right; a steady presence when it matters most. From daily care to unexpected moments, our school nurses help keep students safe, supported, & ready to learn. Today, we recognize them for the work they do every day. #WeAreCentral “
Later on May 6, Central 301 shared a tradition involving graduating seniors: ” Back where it all began… Each year, our Central High School seniors return to their grade schools to take one more photo—this time in caps and gowns. Last week this group dropped by Lily Lake #WeAreCentral “
Central Community Unit School District 301 includes several schools such as Central High School and Lily Lake Grade School and serves students in Kane and DeKalb counties ( Illinois Report Card ). The district employs 280 teachers who earn an average salary of $58,199 before pension contributions; women make up nearly four-fifths of the teaching staff ( Illinois Report Card ). Demographically, the student body is predominantly White (65.3%), with Hispanic (16.5%), Asian (12.2%), and Black (2.1%) representation ( Illinois Report Card ).
In terms of finances and attendance, Central Community Unit School District 301 spent $19,244 per student in 2020 for a total expenditure of over $84 million ( Illinois Report Card ). The chronic truancy rate within the district stands at 1.9 percent—significantly below the statewide average—reflecting lower absenteeism among enrolled students ( Illinois Report Card ).
